title: What Does Vision Tool-Use Reinforcement Learning Really Learn? Disentangling Tool-Induced and Intrinsic Effects for Crop-and-Zoom
claim: A coarse-to-fine framework separates intrinsic gains from tool-induced effects, decomposes them into gain and harm terms, and diagnoses mechanisms.
layout: 4 lettered panels (a-d), mixed grid, cascading top-to-bottom; equation links panels c and d
description: A four-panel figure for the MED framework. Panel a, at top left, shows an alpaca mascot trained with Vision Tool RL and then evaluated two ways: a tool-free path (Acc_wo, alpaca with a book) and a tool-available path (Acc_w, alpaca with a magnifying glass). Panel b, at bottom left, plots performance drift against steps with shaded areas for intrinsic capability and tool-induced gain. Panel c, at top right, is the largest panel. It shows grids of red and green checkmark and cross cells at t=0 and t=T, with a legend. Under the grids, an equation for G(t) splits into four probability terms with small icons. Dashed orange arrows lead from each term to panel d, which has four small line plots of probability over steps: Call Gain, Schema Gain, Call Harm and Schema Harm. The eye goes first to the colorful grids and the equation.
caption: The MED (Measure--Explain--Diagnose) framework for vision tool-use RL. (a) We train a VLM with tool-use RL and evaluate each checkpoint under two protocols: tool-free accuracy $Acc_{\mathrm{wo}}$ (tool-free performance) and tool-available accuracy $Acc_{\mathrm{w}}$. (b) Measure: separate tool-free drift $f_{\mathrm{wo}}(t)=Acc_{\mathrm{wo}}(t)-Acc_{\mathrm{wo}}(0)$ from tool-induced drift $\Delta_{\mathrm{tool}}(t)$ by tracking the evolution of the gap $G(t)=Acc_{\mathrm{w}}(t)-Acc_{\mathrm{wo}}(t)$. (c) Explain: decompose $G(t)$ into Gains on tool-free failures $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fail}}(t)$ and Harms on tool-free successes $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{succ}}(t)$, further distinguishing tool-call effects from no-call effects under tool availability (four terms to the right of the equal sign). (d) Diagnose: probe the underlying mechanisms behind each term's evolution to identify what changes in tool use drive gains or harms.
abstract: Vision tool-use reinforcement learning (RL) can equip vision language models with visual operators such as crop-and-zoom and achieves strong performance gains, yet it remains unclear whether these gains are driven by improvements in tool use or evolving intrinsic capabilities. We introduce MED (Measure--Explain--Diagnose), a coarse-to-fine framework that disentangles intrinsic capability changes from tool-induced effects, decomposes the tool-induced performance difference into gain and harm terms, and probes the mechanisms driving their evolution. Across checkpoint-level analyses in the crop-and-zoom setting on two VLMs with different tool priors and six benchmarks, we find that improvements are dominated by intrinsic learning, while tool-use RL mainly reduces tool-induced harm (e.g., fewer call-induced errors and weaker tool schema interference) and yields limited progress in tool-based correction of intrinsic failures. Overall, in the crop-and-zoom setting studied here, current vision tool-use RL learns to coexist safely with tools rather than master them.
